peopleAlsoAsk.question: Does Karenia brevis cause red tide?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Red tide is one type of harmful algal bloom that is caused by high concentrations of toxic dinoflagellates, microscopic algae. In Florida and the Gulf of Mexico, the alga that causes most red tides is Karenia brevis, often abbreviated as K. brevis.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What is Karenia for?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Globally distributed genus of athecate, bloom forming dinoflagellates. Causes red tide on a near annual basis along Florida, Texas, and Mexico coasts. Produces the neurotoxin brevetoxin, which may lead to: Human poisonings (Neurotoxic Shellfish Poisoning, NSP)
peopleAlsoAsk.title: Karenia - Harmful Algal Blooms

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What toxins are in Karenia brevis sulcata?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: At least one species, K. brevis, produces brevetoxin that not only kills fish, marine mammals, and other animals, but also causes Neurotoxic Shellfish Poisoning and respiratory distress in humans. The lipid soluble brevetoxin can biomagnify up the food chain through fish to top carnivores like dolphins, killing them.
peopleAlsoAsk.title: KARENIA: The biology and ecology of a toxic genus - PMC - NIH

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What does Karenia look like?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Karenia are naked, flat, unicellular, photosynthetic cells that are quite pleomorphic: size tends to range from about 20–90 um. The cell contains a straight apical groove, and differences in apical grooves (acrobases) are often used to distinguish between species.
